relation_to_B3: B3 used a tangential velocity damper and made slip worse (slip max 11.05 -> 82.9 cold, 6.94 -> 36.2 assist). That law was WRONG as an adhesion model: adhesion is a normal attachment force that raises friction, not a tangential damper. B3 numbers stand as recorded; nothing is re-tuned.

channel.name: adhesion_normal
channel.force_law: F = -A * z_hat applied at the contact point of every tarsus that is already in contact with the floor, i.e. a declared attachment that presses the foot into the substrate
channel.magnitude: A = 0.5 W per loaded foot, W = the model's own weight
channel.active_when: that leg has at least one tarsus-floor contact
channel.why_this_shape: this is the functional form of the official adhesion actuator: it does not push the body sideways, it only holds the foot against the substrate so that the existing Coulomb friction can carry the tangential load
channel.declared_bound_rationale: 0.5 W per foot is a declared engineering bound, not a calibrated adhesion value; absolute SI remains NOT_ESTABLISHED

unchanged: gravity, timestep, solver, contacts, joint ranges, actuator gains, torque limits

acceptance_for_this_probe.question: same as B3: does grip bring per-leg material slip under 0.5 with support above 0.9 and COM above 1.2?
acceptance_for_this_probe.decision_rule: report grip OFF and ON side by side; no post-hoc tuning of A or the activation rule
acceptance_for_this_probe.labelling: ON = derived-channel, OFF = frozen-body; never mixed
